summary.text: 前 commonly means ‘in front,’ ‘forward,’ and ‘before.’ A reported account analyzes the related graph 歬 as 止 above 舟, representing a boat moving forward; a competing account says a graph associated with cutting was reused for the directional word. The evidence does not settle which graph came first.

formation.text: The traditional analysis of 歬 is a semantic compound: 止 above 舟 depicts or evokes a boat moving forward. This analysis is recorded for 歬 and does not establish 前’s origin. A competing account associates 前 with a cutting graph and proposes that it was later used for the directional word; this graph history remains disputed.

components.text: In the related graph 歬, 止 is placed above 舟 in the account of a boat moving forward. This is a pictorial part of that reported scene, not a proven component of 前.
In 歬, 舟 represents the boat in the reported picture of forward movement. This analysis belongs to 歬, not the current graph 前.

history.text: 前 is recorded in bronze forms, including a form indexed to Western Zhou material, and in small-seal script. These records document graph forms but do not date the first lexical use.

Historical accounts disagree: one treats 歬 as the directional graph and 前 as a later way to write its word; another associates 前 with cutting and treats 歬 as the older directional form. The sequence is unresolved.

In the cutting account, a sign associated with cutting was reused to write the directional word because the words were said to sound alike or similarly. This is proposed borrowing between words, not a demonstrated change in meaning. No independent name and pronunciation for a depicted implement are established, so the sound match remains unverified; 前’s reconstructed reading alone cannot prove it.
A separate account analyzes 剪 as 刀 plus 歬 serving as a sound element. Sources also record cutting-related uses written with 前, but do not establish a sequence leading to the modern forms.

uncertainties.text: The accounts disagree over whether 歬 or a graph involving 刀 came first in the history of directional 前; the sequence remains unresolved.
The cited uses do not securely date the earliest lexical use or establish the order of the motion, spatial, and temporal senses.
The proposed cutting-related borrowing lacks an independently established name and pronunciation for the depicted implement, so the sound match remains unverified.
Written descriptions support discussion of reported forms and analyses, but no character-specific glyph image is included.

senses.text: 前 is used for a position in front and for forward direction. The evidence does not securely date the historical emergence of these uses.
前 also means earlier in time or preceding. Its historical development in relation to the spatial sense is not established.

developments.text: Spatial and temporal uses are documented, but their relationship and chronology are not established.

limitations.text: Bronze and seal-form records do not date the first lexical use or establish an earliest meaning for 前. Forward motion is a reported interpretation of 歬, not a proven original sense of 前.
The cutting use may concern a distinct word written with the same graph. The proposed sound-based borrowing is not demonstrated by an independently attested object-name comparison.

overview.text: In one account, 歬 has 止 above 舟, picturing a boat moving forward. A competing account says a cutting graph was reused for the directional word because the words sounded alike; the proposed sound match is unverified. 前 commonly means ‘in front’ or ‘before.’

components.text: In 歬, 止 appears above 舟 in the account of a boat moving forward.
舟 is the boat in that account of 歬.

relationships.text: A dictionary identifies 歬 as a variant of 前. This records a graphic relationship without deciding which form is historically earlier.

evidence.text: Depicts a boat (舟) moving (止) forward (前).
不行而進謂之歬。从止在舟上。

Originally 歬, an ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 止 (“foot”) + 舟 (“boat”) – a foot on a boat moving forward.
In the current form, 止 is simplified to 䒑 and 舟 to 月. The current form with an additional 刀 (“knife”) (𠝣 > 𣦃 > 前) is the original form of 剪 (OC *ʔslenʔ, “to cut”).
Unrelated to 俞.
Unknown (Schuessler, 2007).

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00355-003 research note; variant relationship 歬/前
evidence.text: The entry treats 歬 as a variant of 前 and quotes Shuowen: 歬 means moving forward and is formed from 止 over 舟. It also records a competing traditional explanation: 刀+歬 was the graph for cutting evenly, later written 前 in clerical form; 歬 was then used for the directional word. Guangyun is cited as calling 歬 an old form of 前. This source reports competing historical lexicographic accounts; it does not resolve which graph was first.
evidence.title: A00355-003 歬 (前) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: character evolution and cited inscription forms
evidence.text: The database lists 前 in bronze inscriptions (including bronze collection entries dated to Western Zhou) and in Shuowen small seal script. It describes 止 above 舟 as indicating a boat moving forward. This corroborates the graph components and a forward-motion interpretation in the bronze/seal record, but its page does not establish the earliest semantic stage or explain the separate 剪 analysis.
evidence.title: 漢字「前」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢典 (ZDIC), quoting Shuowen and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.field: Shuowen entry for 歬 and commentary
evidence.text: The quoted Shuowen entry reads, in paraphrase, “moving forward is called 歬; formed from 止 on 舟.” Duan Yucai's note says later writers used 前, the graph associated with even cutting, for the directional word 歬, and used 翦 for cutting evenly. This explicitly distinguishes competing graph histories and a word/graph borrowing account; it supplies no independent pronunciation for a depicted tool or knife-name.
evidence.title: 前 qián、jiǎn - 汉典

evidence.text: The entry lists bronze forms, Chu manuscripts, Qin manuscripts, Shuowen seal form and Han clerical form; its visible bronze examples include Western Zhou middle and late inscriptions. It gives motion-forward as the basic verbal sense, cites 《广雅》 “前，进也,” and lists directional/front and earlier-in-time senses with citations such as 《诗·邶风·简兮》 and 《礼记·檀弓》. It also lists 前通翦 ‘cut/trim’ with a 《韩非子·八经》 citation. The page gives no securely dated earliest occurrence for each sense, and received-text citations are not themselves dated physical attestations.
evidence.title: 前 qián、jiǎn - 汉典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 剪 entry, Shuowen graph analysis and sense
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen's 剪 as “齊斷也。从刀，歬聲” (cut evenly; from 刀, with 歬 as phonetic). It says Shuowen wrote the cutting character as 前 and that the common modern graph is 剪. This supports 歬 as a sound component in this character according to Shuowen, but it does not establish the pronunciation/name of any depicted object in 前's graph.
evidence.title: A00364 剪 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: Kangxi citation on the cutting graph and written forms
evidence.text: The entry reports the 《正字通》 claim that 𠝣 is the original graph of 剪 and quotes Shuowen's analysis of the cutting graph as 刀 plus 歬 phonetic. It also reports the gloss ‘knife name’ in a Du Fu citation, but gives no historical reconstruction or evidence that a particular depicted implement was named with a sound matching 前. Thus a loan/graph-history theory about 前 and 剪 cannot be justified merely by reconstructing 前's pronoun or citing this later gloss.
evidence.title: 𠝣的解释|𠝣的意思|汉典“𠝣”字的基本解释

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

The Ministry dictionary and Shuowen-derived tradition conflict over whether 歬 (止 over 舟) is the original directional graph, or whether a graph with 刀 was the cutting word and 前 was borrowed for direction. The materials support reporting the disagreement, not resolving chronology.

The proposed relationship between the source word for ‘cut’ and any depicted tool/knife object remains under-evidenced. No independent original object name or pronunciation was recovered; a reconstruction of 前 alone would not prove that borrowing claim.

A direct Unihan lookup for 舟 (U+821F), 剪 (U+526A), and 歬 (U+6B6C) failed in the web tool. No component modern readings or full official record for these inspected entries are asserted. The supplied local dataset contains exact rows only for 前.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart row for 前 was checked, but no corresponding local Baxter–Sagart row for a proposed sound component was supplied or verified. No reconstructed phonetic comparison is claimed.

The currently verified attested meanings include forward motion, spatial ‘in front’, temporal ‘before/earlier’, guiding/leading, and reported graph/sense use for cutting. Their exact historical order and semantic transitions are not established by the available character-specific citations.

No primary dated inscription passage establishing the earliest lexical sense or its chronology was verified. The Academia Sinica record supplies a bronze-form index and a later seal form, but not a dated earliest semantic attestation.

The proposed cutting-related loan cannot be demonstrated from 前’s reconstructed pronunciation alone: no independent original object name and pronunciation were established here.

No external exact character-reading row for 舟, 剪, or 歬 was verified. Local dataset information supplied in the input is not external evidence; component pronunciation comparisons are therefore not asserted.
